topic.title: Intel® Total Memory Encryption - Multi-Key (MKTME) Overview

body.p: TME (Total Memory Encryption) introduced in 11th Generation of CPUs aims at mitigating the cold boot attack. In such an attack the adversary goal is to retrieve secrets stored in volatile memory. A simplified flavor of the attack works as follows:

The attack works in the environment where the system state is in standby (i.e. S3) such that the DRAM is still powered. The adversary would freeze the DDR DIMMs while in standby. Thereafter, the DDR DIMMs are detached from the victim's system and re-attached to the adversary's system. The adversary powers on their system to be able to steal information from the victim's DRAM. Because the data in the DDR DIMMS are stored as plain the adversary can retrieve the data with ease. The Total Memory Protection can provide mitigation with such attack by encrypting all of memory in the DDR DIMMS.
The MKTME builds upon the baseline TME technology to support multiple encryption keys (Multi-Key TME, or MKTME) with ability to use specific key at a memory page granularity.
